notes:
Account brief: HarborTrace is a EU-headquartered financial regtech vendor evaluating Redwood Private VPC for production inference. Primary drivers: strict data residency (EU-only), end-to-end audit trail, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Key ask: exportable audit logs (structured JSON + CEF option) to corporate Splunk instance via Fluentd/Logstash or S3 drop with manifest.

Security/compliance snippets: 
- Compliance team requires retention policy: hot access for 12 months, cold archive immutable for 7 years (regulatory).
- Log types needed: admin auth events, model inference requests (metadata only: request_id, model_id, prompt hash, token count, latency), streaming session start/stop, KV-cache hits/misses (anonymized), rollout & fallback events, quota/limit alerts, error stacks.
- Access logs: per-IP & service-account, TLS mutual auth events, SAML IdP assertions masked in logs, admin console actions (who/when/what).
- Tamper-evidence: log signatures + sequential HMAC recommended by compliance.
- SIEM export: preferred formats JSON (schema v1), CEF for legacy, syslog/HTTPS endpoints to Splunk HEC. Must support backfill and replays with idempotency markers.
- Key management: need CMK integration with AWS KMS + HSM-backed key policy; require key rotation policy and proof of envelope encryption. Also evaluate on-prem HSM connector for air-gapped option.

Recent activity / timeline: 
- 2025-08-15: inbound lead (growth), initial discovery call (Maya) — captured infra constraints.
- 2025-09-02: technical scoping email thread started (Jonah).
- 2025-10-10: product demo — emphasis on dedicated vs private differences; compliance flagged audit logging requirements.
- 2025-11-04: security questionnaire (SSQ) submitted by HarborTrace; they requested sample log schemas.
- 2025-12-01: architecture workshop — discussed SIEM export patterns, network topology (VPC peering vs private link). Action: Redwood to provide sample fluentd config + S3 lifecycle doc.
- 2026-02-18: demo follow-up w/ Fireflies call ff-2026-02-18-HTC-demo-91 — CTO present; asked about immutable retention and tamper evidence.
- 2026-03-09: pre-PoC sync; HarborTrace legal sent DPA redlines.

PoC scope requested by customer: 
- Stand up Private VPC deployment in eu-west-1 w/ VPC endpoints.
- Deliver sample auditing pipeline: ingestion to Splunk HEC and parallel S3 archival in eu-central-1; include sample log schema (JSON) and Fluentd config.
- Demonstrate CMK usage for token-level metadata encryption (envelope) and key rotation.
- Provide SLA for log delivery and estimates for cold archive throughput.

Open questions / engineering concerns: 
- Need to confirm the exact fields in the inference event schema — compliance wants to avoid PII in logs, so we need a scrubbed prompt hash approach.
- Performance impact of enabled detailed audit logging on p99 latency and cost. Suggest toggles: minimal, standard, verbose.
- Who will manage Splunk ingestion keys and network egress (customer preferred: private link + HEC inside their VPC).

Next steps (short): 
- Send over canonical JSON log schema v1 and Fluentd sample by 2026-03-15 (Jonah).
- Book security workshop with HarborTrace compliance + Redwood infra (target week of 2026-03-22).
- Legal to reciprocate on DPA redlines; ask for prioritized list of redlines to triage.

Sales notes / stakeholder map: 
- Primary buyer: CTO (Martin Leroux) — cares about KMS and tamper-evidence.
- Compliance lead: Elena Fischer — owns retention policy and log schema signoff.
- Platform lead: SRE manager (Khalid Rahman) — cares about throughput, peering, and Splunk connectivity.
- Procurement: expects enterprise contract + 12 month commit for Dedicated/Private.

- "If you can show HSM-backed key flow + signed logs we can move to PO" — Martin
- "PoC must not expose raw prompts in logs; hash + salt approach preferred" — Khalid
